messages:
tara: Noticed a bunch of small inconsistencies while fixing links in the quickstarts: we have both `embedding` and `vector` used interchangeably. Proposing we standardize on `embedding` in prose and keep `vector` only when discussing math. Thoughts?

chris: +1 for 'embedding' as the user-facing term. 'vector' feels too mathy for most readers. Can we add a glossary entry clarifying both?

lee: Agreed. Also found `model_family` vs `model` in several SDK snippets. That one could be confusing. Do we prefer `model` everywhere and reserve `model_family` for architecture-level docs?

tara: My preference: docs & quickstarts -> `model`; architecture/ops -> `model_family`. I'll draft a tiny rubric and add to STYLEGUIDE.md.

yneil: Small microcopy note: quickstarts should use imperative verbs and keep examples minimal. E.g., change "You can call the API" -> "Call the API". Also prefer present tense.

tara: Good. I'll include a 2-sentence rule: "Use present tense, active voice. Limit each step to one action."

chris: For the actual edits, can we avoid changing code that might be copy-pasted by customers? i.e., don't rename public SDK parameter names. Only change comments, sample variable names, and prose.

tara: Absolutely. Changes limited to docs text and example variables that are clearly not part of a published SDK API. I'll list every file changed in the PR.

docs-ci: preflight checklist: 1) run linkcheck 2) run docs linter 3) run snippet compile tests (TS/Python) 4) add glossary entries + redirects 5) ping SDK owners

tara: Example before/after for TS snippet I'll include in PR description: 

```ts
// BEFORE
const vector = await client.createEmbedding({model: "rwd-embed-1", input: text})
// AFTER (docs-only variable rename)
const embedding = await client.createEmbedding({model: "rwd-embed-1", input: text})
```

chris: Nice. Can we also add a CI step that verifies that only comments and local variable names changed and nothing in exported types? I can add a tiny git-diff filter script for the PR.

yneil: Here's a grep-friendly filter I use to detect exported API changes: 

```bash
# list lines that change exported declarations
git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | xargs rg "^export (const|function|type|interface|class)" -n || true
```

tara: Perfect. I'll wire that into the PR checklist.

lee: Also: add redirects for old glossary terms so links don't 404. E.g., /docs/vocab/vector -> /docs/vocab/embedding.

tara: Will add. I'll open the PR now and include: file list, before/after snippets, the STYLEGUIDE.md microcopy paragraph, the glossary additions, CI filter, and the docs-ci checklist. Tagging @chris and @yneil for review.

chris: Reviewing when it's up. Thanks for doing the tidy. :tada:

yneil: LGTM once CI rules are in place.

docs-ci: PR template reminder: mark changes as "docs-only" where appropriate and include a short migration note for any deprecated wording.

tara: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 (draft). Comments welcome.
